summary.source: Fresh Session 87 audit of the live main worktree after mandatory Studio OS propagation. The audit began with the six explicitly preserved S86 findings and re-verified every premise against current source. The salary-cap premise was also executed against a fixed-seed 32-team league: cap space ranged from $89,994,526 to $110,932,923, mean $100,924,043, with 0/32 teams below $25M. The other five premises were confirmed by following the actual source-to-runtime-to-browser path rather than trusting renderer or engine declarations.
summary.qualityBar: L2 for every item. Every gameplay correction must be observable in the browser and pinned by focused behavior coverage. Salary calibration must be distribution-tested across real generated leagues, keep all fresh teams legal at kickoff, and preserve signed contracts in existing saves. No item may weaken the public-launch HOLD, add variable-cost runtime, add a dependency, or move identity away from Obelisk.

profile.rubric: product rubric plus game-medium overlay and app-release-gate: consequential General Manager decisions, simulation truth, mobile/theme parity, static-host safety, exact staging identity, rollback, privacy, and honest independent launch holds
profile.staging: stable GitHub/Cloudflare Pages staging must prove the exact immutable candidate before direct-to-main production promotion; public sanitization and CANON-053 rendered-pixel evidence are mandatory
profile.source: arc profile, S86 handoff, live canon adoption, current source tree, fixed-seed GameSession probes, DOM-id cross-checks, and current deployment receipts

gameLoopReview.evidence: S86 restored the weekly tactic, draft pick, and aging curve, but S87 measured the next load-bearing fiction: the $255M salary cap cannot currently constrain a single opening roster. Two authored pressure systems are unreachable, and four visible evidence surfaces either lose their source or have no mount. No real cohort exists, so retention remains unproven rather than inferred from feature count.

releaseGate.deploymentVerdict: CONDITIONAL GO after all six items, full verification, exact stable staging, rollback proof, and a fresh app-release-gate pass.
releaseGate.launchVerdict: NO-GO. Preserve launchReady false and the public-launch HOLD.
launchHolds: SHA-bound public-launch approval distinct from this technical deploy authorization
registered and end-to-end verified external Obelisk relying party before account-bearing flows

releaseTruth: all gameplay changes source-bound and rendered before candidate promotion

recommendedMoves: Make scarcity real first: replace the nearly linear contract formula with one versioned market curve whose fixed-seed distribution puts most opening teams inside a meaningful cap-management band without starting any team illegal.

Repair the consequence chain next: adapt live team chemistry, owner patience/expectation, and season records into the exact shapes consumed by narrative and fan-pressure systems, with end-to-end tests proving the player can actually receive and answer the authored pressure.

Finish at the evidence boundary: use max semantics for long plays, project player identity onto waivers, and mount the already-authored Franchise Legends and GM Reputation renderers; then inspect every affected surface in both themes and both target viewports.

preverifiedSkips.candidate: new AI coach or paid inference layer
preverifiedSkips.reason: Rejected. The game is intentionally zero-backend for its core loop, no AI capability gap blocks these findings, and adding variable-cost inference would violate the free-tier discipline without improving the measured defects.

Rejected for this audit. No new account-bearing flow is being introduced, franchise command authorization is already centralized, and public launch remains held on external Obelisk relying-party proof rather than replaced with local auth.

preverifiedSkips.candidate: raise the salary cap or lower cap-alert thresholds
preverifiedSkips.reason: Rejected as force-green. The $255M league rule is the declared authority; the defect is the salary distribution beneath it. Alert thresholds already reveal the problem honestly.
Rejected. Existing saves keep their negotiated agreements; the versioned market curve applies to newly generated or newly signed contracts and becomes binding through normal contract turnover.

preverifiedSkips.candidate: replace player IDs inside the persistent waiver ledger
preverifiedSkips.reason: Rejected. Player IDs are the correct durable authority. The browser-facing dashboard projection should join names/position/overall without duplicating mutable player data in saves.

preverifiedSkips.candidate: launch readiness from technical deployment success
preverifiedSkips.reason: Rejected. Technical deploy authorization is independent from Zoho receipt/reply proof, lifecycle authority, founder public-launch approval, and Obelisk relying-party verification.

items.category: Franchise economy / decision consequence / simulation realism
items.title: Turn the salary cap from decorative headroom into the core roster-building constraint
items.premise: The declared salary cap is $255M, but buildContract prices a 99 OVR player at only about 3.2 times a 55 OVR player and initial player generation caps salary at $19.5M. A fixed-seed live league measured all 32 opening teams between $89,994,526 and $110,932,923 of cap space, mean $100,924,043; not one team was within $25M of the cap. Tag, restructure, rollover, cap alerts, contract negotiation and cut decisions therefore exist around a constraint that never binds.
evidence: src/config.js declares salaryCap 255,000,000 and maxSalary 45,000,000
src/domain/contracts.js computes overall^2 * 580, making the configured maximum unreachable
src/domain/playerFactory.js further caps every opening contract at 19,500,000
items.constraint: Use a versioned, monotonic market curve; preserve existing signed contracts; keep every fresh opening roster legal; preserve min/max rules and deterministic RNG; expose the pressure through existing cap UI rather than adding backend state.
verification: fixed-seed multi-league test proves a monotonic OVR salary curve with meaningful elite scarcity and reachable configured maximum band
opening-league distribution proves no team starts over the cap and a strong majority starts within a declared competitive cap-space band
existing explicit salary offers and persisted contracts remain unchanged
overview/contract surfaces visibly reflect the corrected cap pressure

L1.recipe: Replace the quadratic default salary with a monotonic cubic-plus-elite curve and remove the opening-roster $19.5M ceiling.

L2.recipe: L1 plus a versioned exported market-salary authority, fixed-seed multi-league distribution tests, explicit existing-contract preservation, and UI-visible cap-pressure proof.

L3.recipe: L2 plus position-market multipliers and a player-facing market-comparison receipt, only after the base distribution remains stable across long-run offseason turnover.

items.category: Narrative engine / General Manager pressure / feedback loop
items.title: Adapt live culture and owner authority into narrative events the General Manager can actually answer
items.premise: checkCultureCrises reads team.worldState.culture.chemistry or team.culture.chemistry, but live teams carry numeric team.chemistry. checkOwnerUltimatums reads hotSeat and owner.mandate, while live ownership authority is patience plus owner.expectation. Both event gates therefore consume shapes the runtime never writes. The authored culture-crisis decision can be unit-tested only by injecting a synthetic event; real play cannot produce it.
evidence: src/engine/narrativeEvents.js reads nested culture chemistry and hotSeat/mandate shapes
src/runtime/GameSession.js refreshChemistryAndSchemeFit writes team.chemistry and team.owner.expectation
test/gm-decision-expansion.test.js injects CULTURE_CRISIS directly rather than reaching it through runNarrativeChecks
the owner ultimatum uses a separate lower-case news record and commitment path, leaving the declared OWNER_ULTIMATUM narrative event unreachable
items.constraint: Do not create a second owner authority or duplicate pressure. Add narrow source adapters so narrative checks consume the fields the runtime already owns; dedupe the existing owner commitment/news path.
verification: a live low-chemistry five-loss team can emit CULTURE_CRISIS through runNarrativeChecks and generate the decision
a live critical owner expectation can emit one OWNER_ULTIMATUM narrative without duplicating the existing commitment or inbox notice
other teams never pressure the controlled General Manager
rendered decision pressure is visible in desktop/mobile dark/light evidence

L1.recipe: Read live team.chemistry and owner patience/expectation as fallbacks in narrativeEvents.

L2.recipe: L1 plus explicit source adapters, owner-event dedupe against the existing ultimatum path, and fixed-seed end-to-end event-to-decision tests.

L3.recipe: L2 plus an executable narrative reachability matrix that proves every declared narrative archetype has a live source path.

items.category: Fan pressure / record authority / weekly feedback
items.title: Make wins and losses move fan approval instead of leaving the entire win band dead
items.premise: updateFanSentiment reads league.latestStandings or league.standings, but GameSession builds standingsRows only as a local dashboard projection and writes neither field to league. The engine therefore passes an empty standings array every week; computeFanApproval defaults every team to .500 and the documented +/-15 win modifier never moves.
evidence: src/engine/fanSentiment.js reads league.latestStandings || league.standings || []
src/runtime/GameSession.js creates standingsRows inside getDashboardState only
team.season already owns live wins/losses at the update boundary
the weekly reason can say won/lost while approval itself ignores the record
items.constraint: Use team.season as the primary live authority with standings only as a compatible override; preserve owner fan-interest and personality modifiers.
verification: same owner context with 8-2 vs 2-8 records yields correctly ordered approval
weekly update uses the live team season without requiring a dashboard render
fan card reason, trend and score stay internally coherent

L1.recipe: Fall back to team.season wins/losses inside computeFanApproval.

L2.recipe: L1 plus explicit record-source precedence, end-to-end weekly tests, and browser-visible score/reason coherence.

L3.recipe: L2 plus bounded expectation bands tied to market/owner context, only with distribution evidence.

items.category: Stat integrity / box score / season records
items.title: Record the longest play as a maximum instead of adding every long play in the game
items.premise: The per-game drive accumulator mergeObject adds every numeric leaf, including passing.long, receiving.long, rushing.long and kicking.long. mergeStats correctly uses max across games, but it receives an already-summed per-game value, producing impossible rows such as a 147-yard longest completion.
evidence: src/engine/gameSimulator.js mergeObject sums all numeric keys
the simulator emits long: yards on every completion, carry, scramble and made field goal
src/domain/playerFactory.js mergeStats already recognizes long as max semantics across games
S86 measured a 147-yard longest completion in live simulation
items.constraint: Change only max-valued stat leaves; every counting and yardage stat must remain additive.
verification: multiple plays in one game retain only the maximum long value
season merge remains maximum across games
passing/receiving/rushing long cannot exceed the longest source play

L1.recipe: Teach the per-game recursive merger that key long uses Math.max.

L2.recipe: L1 plus direct accumulator coverage and a fixed-seed full-game invariant comparing player long stats to play-by-play maxima.

L3.recipe: L2 plus a schema-level registry for additive, max and replace stat semantics across all categories.

items.title: Mount the Franchise Legends and General Manager Reputation views the renderers already author
items.premise: tabHistory calls renderFranchiseLegends('franchiseLegendsContainer', ...), and tabOverview writes gmReputationLabel. Neither ID exists in public/game.html, so both renderers silently no-op. The game computes the dynasty identity and market reputation but never lets the player see either.
evidence: public/lib/tabHistory.js calls franchiseLegendsContainer
public/lib/tabOverview.js calls gmReputationLabel
repo-wide ID search finds neither mount in public/game.html
both renderers guard missing nodes and therefore fail silently
items.constraint: Place each surface in its existing semantic home, keep accessible headings/live regions, and reuse current visual tokens rather than inventing a parallel card system.
verification: DOM contract test proves both IDs exist exactly once
renderer test proves non-empty source data becomes visible
desktop/mobile dark/light screenshots are inspected and hash-bound

L1.recipe: Add the two missing semantic mounts to the GM Legacy card and Dynasty Hall view.

L2.recipe: L1 plus accessible labels, DOM contract coverage, empty-state behavior, and rendered-pixel inspection in both themes/viewports.

L3.recipe: L2 plus cross-linking a legend to the player timeline and reputation to the transaction evidence that earned it.

items.category: UI/UX / roster action clarity / data projection
items.title: Show who is actually on waivers instead of rendering an opaque player ID
items.premise: The persistent waiver ledger correctly stores playerId, release team and expiry, but getDashboardState exposes that raw ledger and tabRoster renders only playerId/releasedBy/week/expires. The waiver table has no player name, position or overall, making the roster decision unreadable even though the player authority is already indexed.
evidence: src/runtime/GameSession.js writes playerId-only waiver ledger entries
getDashboardState exposes this.league.waiverWire without projection
public/lib/tabRoster.js maps the raw rows without joining player identity
the same tab already has player-column decoration utilities for real player rows
items.constraint: Keep IDs as persistent authority; enrich only the dashboard projection from the indexed player record and preserve old saves with missing players.
verification: dashboard waiver rows include id, player, pos and overall for live players
orphaned legacy entries degrade to an explicit unavailable label rather than throw
the browser waiver table renders a clickable/decorated player identity

L1.recipe: Join the dashboard waiver projection against getPlayerById and render player/pos/overall.

L2.recipe: L1 plus orphan-safe projection, player-column decoration, and focused runtime/browser coverage.

L3.recipe: L2 plus claim-priority and cap-impact context beside each player, derived from existing authority.
